title: Predictions come first
plain: The test checks the saved history of the project: the file with our predictions must have been saved before any file with experiment results, and a made-up history where it was saved after must be rejected.
why: A prediction written after seeing the numbers is not a prediction.
done_when: Predictions are older than every result they are compared with, and a reversed or tied history fails.

title: Every setup repeats cleanly
plain: Each setup must have been run twice with the same order, and the two worlds must differ in zero blocks; a setup with no repeat or a differing repeat may not report how many kinds of world it found.
why: If the same order disagrees with itself, differences between orders cannot be believed.
done_when: A missing or differing repeat voids the count and a clean repeat lets it stand.

title: The window is inside the finished area
plain: Every chunk we compare must be close enough to a ticket to be fully built; a window with a corner too far from every ticket must be rejected.
why: Chunks outside the finished area are only partly saved, so comparing them would invent or hide differences.
done_when: All window chunks are within 2 chunks of a ticket in every setup, and the too-wide example fails.

title: Same world means the same everywhere
plain: If world a matches b and b matches c, then a must match c; a table of comparisons that breaks this, or disagrees with the saved fingerprints, is rejected.
why: Grouping orders into kinds of world only makes sense if matching is consistent.
done_when: No measured triple breaks the rule and made-up broken tables fail.

title: No Minecraft files in the repo
plain: The test looks at every file the repo would publish and rejects world saves, level files and server jars, and any result file over 2 MB.
why: Minecraft's files are not ours to publish and the repo should stay small.
done_when: A throwaway repo with such files fails and the real repo has none.

title: Route costs match the rulebook
plain: The new route model must charge the same time for walking, digging with each tool, crafting and smelting as the round 1 rules do.
why: A route is only comparable to round 1 if the same move costs the same.
done_when: Every round 1 move costs the same in the model and in the rules.

title: Waiting does not change the world
plain: Two touching tickets are built once with no wait and once with a one minute wait between them, and the saved blocks in their window must match.
why: If waiting changes the world, a count of kinds of world would count waiting schedules, not orders.
done_when: The two windows have zero differing blocks.
